---

12. Graceful Degradation
------------------------

Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.

| System | Failure mode |
| --- | --- |
| Contentful | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS |
| Global-e | Surface explicit error; do not silently fall back to SFCC for international checkout |
| Didomi | Fail closed — no consent, no third-party scripts |
| Omneo (writes) / Emarsys | Queue and retry silently; never block the user flow |
| Omneo (reads) | **Load-bearing for My Account profile pages** — per DMU-004 only email + Omneo ID are migrated; all other customer profile data is sourced live from Omneo at login. Surface an explicit retry/error UI on profile pages if the round-trip fails; do not render stale or partial profile data. |
| Google Maps | Degrade to manual address entry; never hard-block checkout |
| AP21 (Retail Rewards) | On AP21 unavailability at the point of Rewards application, inform the customer and allow an alternative payment method |
| Narvar (EDD) | Suppress widget; do not show an error or block checkout |

### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment

The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the *spread* of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.

#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)

* **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
* **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.

#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)

`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.

The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):

| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sfcc-scapi` | `<https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`> | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — waiting confirmation from Mani) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `<https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |
| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `<https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
| `google-places` | `<https://places.googleapis.com`> (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |
| `booxi` | Booxi base URL (TBD) | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page. |

**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).

---

13. Testing Strategy
--------------------

Three layers, no duplicated coverage — the cheapest layer that proves a behaviour wins.

| Layer | Tool | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, isolated hooks |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | Single-component user interactions |
| E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries |

### 13.1 What is tested

Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.

### 13.2 E2E gherkin-first workflow

Every Playwright spec starts as a Gherkin `.feature` file that Lead QA validates in plain English before any code is written. This prevents technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour.

### 13.3 Multi-region fixtures

E2E specs are parameterised by `SITE_ID` from day one — every journey runs across all 8 storefronts and 11 active locales, with site-specific `baseUrl`, currency, checkout owner, tax model, and consent default supplied by a fixture rather than hardcoded. (Because a test hardcoded to one region cannot be cheaply expanded later)

### 13.4 Selector priority

Tests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.

---

14. CI/CD & Environments
------------------------

This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.

### 14.1 Topology

A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |

Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

### 14.2 Branch model

GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.

| Branch | Branched from | Merges to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `develop`, `main` | — | protected; PR-only |

Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.

### 14.3 CI workflows

**QA workflow (**`qa.yml`) — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:

* Unit tests (Vitest)
* Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)

**SIT gate (**`digital-sit.yml`) — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:

* Playwright `p0` priority specs
* Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
* Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
* Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
* Trend gate against the LHCI history server

### 14.4 Deployment

Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:

* **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
* **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
* **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
* **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
* **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions

Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.

MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`.",

1. Core Tell No Lies scope from requirements and docs

[Zimmermann Functional Requirements(Analytics & AB Testing) (1)](https://ts.accenture.com/sites/Zimmerman/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B54874C0D-9CFF-43D6-BE6F-EA4C741032CF%7D&file=Zimmermann%20Functional%20Requirements(Analytics%20%26%20AB%20Testing)%20(1).csv&action=default&mobileredirect=true&DefaultItemOpen=1) says AAB-002 requires a well-structured data layer as the single source of truth for downstream analytics and marketing tags across the shopping journey. # Integration Open Items — Consolidated

> This is an aggregate of `.docs/integration` open items.

Open items requiring client confirmation across the fifteen external integrations in scope for the Zimmermann PWA storefront. Each item is a decision, contract, credential, or sign-off that must land before the corresponding integration can be implemented end-to-end against a real account.

## Summary

We need their documentations or implementation guide for at least:
Omneo iframe (for communication preferences), Booxi, MuleSoft (for GiveX balance check, order history/detail, returns).

Then for all the external systems (also incl. Adyen, Global-e, Google Maps, reCAPTCHA, Narvar, Didomi, GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Measmerize) we'll need their relevant Zimmermann-specific IDs, for each environment (dev/uat/prod etc) if applicable, and their associated Didomi feature/vendor ID if consent-gated.

Plus:

- GiveX: Do we need reCAPTCHA for balance check?
- CAI-023 Can MuleSoft aggregate stock?

| #   | Integration | Items                  |
| --- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
| 1   | SFCC        | 2                      |
| 2   | Contentful  | 3                      |
| 3   | MuleSoft    | 4                      |
| 4   | Omneo       | 3 (all hard blockers)  |
| 5   | GiveX       | 3                      |
| 6   | Booxi       | 4 (scope/timeline TBC) |
| 7   | Adyen       | 2                      |
| 8   | Global-e    | 2                      |
| 9   | Google Maps | 1                      |
| 10  | reCAPTCHA   | 2                      |
| 11  | Narvar      | 2                      |
| 12  | Didomi      | 2                      |
| 13  | GTM         | 2                      |
| 14  | Inside Chat | 2                      |
| 15  | Optimizely  | 1                      |
| 16  | Crazy Egg   | 3                      |
| 17  | Measmerize  | 1                      |
| 18  | Vimeo       | 2                      |

Total: 41 items across 18 integrations.

---

## 1. SFCC

1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.

2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) assumes `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to a different origin than the SCAPI host (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). If they share an origin the two pools should be merged.

## 2. Contentful

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.

## 3. MuleSoft

1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
4. **CAI-023 — warehouse + boutique stock aggregation for browse-level availability.** Confirm whether MuleSoft can deliver a pre-aggregated available-to-promise figure combining warehouse and eligible boutique stock, to drive the Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock states on PDP and PLP. If MuleSoft cannot pre-aggregate, the storefront must decide whether to request both sources separately and aggregate client-side (extra round-trip) or fall back to SFCC-only inventory. This is distinct from the cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) and the Find in Boutique flyout (CAI-038), both of which have their own endpoints. **Owner:** Integration team (Tryzens / MuleSoft).

## 4. Omneo

No Omneo-issued identifiers, hosts, or credentials are currently in Accenture's possession. All three items below are needed before implementation can begin against a real Omneo tenant; all three are hard blockers.

1. **Communication Preferences iFrame — confirm the non-Shopify auth handshake.** CRM-174 confirms the screen is rendered as an Omneo iFrame; the iFrame contains Communication Preferences, region/country selection (location, state, and language preference), and three clickable images that open the respective PLP within the iFrame (PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is an enhancement, not in scope for launch). Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. However, Omneo's documented embed is a Shopify theme extension that authenticates via the Omneo CX Shopify app proxy, which a PWA does not have. Confirm, for the non-Shopify embed on Zimmermann's plan: the Profile Portal embed URL, how the Communication Preferences and region/country selection views are scoped within it, and the auth handshake outside Shopify (a customer-scoped signed-URL / HMAC approach, or a server-minted customer-scoped token). If no embed path is available, the fallback is a redirect to the hosted portal or a native rebuild against Omneo's API.
2. **Omneo identifiers and embed URL.** Provide the values needed to construct the iFrame `src` for production and each non-production environment:
   - Omneo tenant / account identifier (the value that appears in the embed URL, e.g. the account subdomain or path slug)
   - Exact embed URL host(s) and path(s) for the Communication Preferences widget — needed both to build the iFrame and to add to the storefront's `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` and `connect-src` allowlist
   - Any other public identifier the widget requires (widget ID, environment ID, configuration key)
3. **HMAC signing secret (or token mechanism).** Provide the per-environment secret/credential Omneo issues for the customer-scoped embed auth. Without it the Omneo ID proxy authentication cannot be exercised end-to-end; until it is provided, the integration can only be developed against a mock.

## 5. GiveX

1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** The integration team to publish the request and response schema for the MuleSoft balance-check endpoint (`POST /givex/balance` placeholder) — the request carries both the card number and the PIN (secure PINs are enabled) — plus the error taxonomy that maps GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, including the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the storefront cannot implement the call against a real MuleSoft instance. **Owner:** MuleSoft — GiveX supplies the underlying failure-code list; Zimmermann owns the final customer-facing message copy.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route. **Owner:** MuleSoft (host / token / thresholds); the MRT-edge WAF / bot / rate-limit config is ours.
3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT balance-check route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request — this is not yet decided. If a CAPTCHA is used, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login (no new provisioning). **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## 6. Booxi

Boutique appointment history is a PWA-direct read (PWA → MRT → Booxi); scope and timeline are TBC.

1. **Storefront scope and timeline (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope, and confirm the target sprint. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments — whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC / Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

## 7. Adyen

1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.

## 8. Global-e

1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply: (a) the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers; and (b) the `postMessage` schema and trusted sender origin for iframe resize and order-completion signals — the PWA listener must verify `event.origin` against this value before acting. Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order, to decide between rendering full order detail or a "View on tracking page" fallback. Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

## 9. Google Maps

1. **Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project and per-environment API keys.** Zimmermann to provision one Places API key per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.). Without the keys the integration cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

## 10. reCAPTCHA

1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only, for MRT token verification) per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK. Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

## 11. Narvar

1. **Per-environment Narvar retailer ID and CONVERT API key.** Provide one set per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.). Without these, the widget cannot be exercised against a real Narvar account.

2. **Didomi consent category for Narvar Promise.** Confirm which Didomi category the CONVERT widget falls under (Performance?). This determines whether the widget loads for EU and UK users who accept Performance cookies but decline Analytics or Marketing.

## 12. Didomi

1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs, the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.

## 13. GTM (with Tell No Lies/Zimm)

1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). Zimmermann/Accenture to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** The data layer is a single shared artifact. Tell No Lies to confirm the storefront's proposed event and attribute schema (page views, product impressions, add-to-cart, begin-checkout, purchase and related ecommerce events, plus consent state and user identifiers) satisfies both GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) and the frontend-direct data-layer consumers (Optimizely, Crazy Egg — not GTM tags). Any additional attributes Optimizely needs for segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg needs for filtering (AAB-005) must be raised at this point.

## 14. Inside Chat

1. **The script tag.** From Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens (the equivalent of what Tryzens hardcoded in Magento).
2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Inside Chat is now a direct PWA head tag (not via GTM — confirmed 2026-07-10). Zimmermann to provide the Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

## 15. Optimizely (with Zimm/TNL)

Optimizely Web is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent.

1. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Optimizely (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 16. Crazy Egg (with Zimm/TNL)

Crazy Egg (heatmaps / session recording) is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm).

1. **Crazy Egg account / site ID per environment.** Zimmermann to provide the account / site ID (script), confirming whether a single account serves all environments or one per tier.
2. **Masking configuration ownership.** Confirm that Tell No Lies owns and applies the session-recording masking configuration (payment and PII fields suppressed) inside the Crazy Egg application. The storefront-side scope is confirmed (AAB-005): the PWA populates the data layer and renders maskable fields with stable selectors; masking itself is outside the PWA.
3. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Crazy Egg (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 17. Measmerize

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## 18. Vimeo

Vimeo is used for product video (PDP) and editorial video (content pages via Contentful CMS). The embed loads client-side as a facade-loaded iframe.

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — suppresses Vimeo's tracking cookies, no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." Zimmermann to confirm before PDP video implementation begins. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

# TNL Data Dictionary & Data Layer Review — FED walk-in kit
**7 Aug 2026, 15:30–16:30 · organiser: Lucy Fu · you hold the FED line (with Tim, Architect)**
Room: Andrew Arnott (TNL/analytics, Director) · Vicky Routley (Zimm Digital Perf) · Rebecca Jourdan · Emma Kirwan · Tim Lavelle (ACN Arch) · Jasmijn Tsang · Bianca Morley · Natasha Lay · Isabel Chaloner · you.
This is the follow-up to the 13-07 "Data Dictionary/GTM" session (you attended; not transcribed). TNL walks through the DD + Data Layer artefacts "completed to date."

---

## Your opening line
> "FED scope is **AAB-002: the PWA emits a native, first-party data layer to the Data Dictionary TNL defines. TNL consumes it in GTM/Addingwell and owns every tag, trigger and downstream route.** The data layer fires **regardless of consent**; Didomi gates at the **tag** layer. What I need out of today is the **final DD published + jointly validated as implementable**, so we can lock the event/attribute schema and unblock both our emission build and TNL's GTM utility."

## The ownership model — now resolved (was the 13-07 "grey area")
Reconciled from the FR CSV (TNL/Zimm = "Define the Data Dictionary, configure GTM/Addingwell to consume"; Accenture = "implement GTM tag + correct data-layer mapping on the storefront"), Tim's 5-Jun statement ("the DD defines attributes & keys, then we create a script to trigger dataLayer updates per the DD"), and repo `analytics.md`/`13-gtm.md`:

| Layer | Owner | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Data Dictionary (the spec)** | **TNL defines / owns** | The artefact walked through today. FED **reviews + validates implementability**, does not author it. |
| **2. Data-layer emission (the code)** | **Accenture / FED implements** | `dataLayer.push()` at each lifecycle event, native in SFCC/PWA (AAB-002, JIRA **SFCC-553**). |
| **3. GTM + Addingwell + downstream tags** | **TNL owns entirely** | Container `GTM-M8PJ5D`, hosted on Addingwell (`ruffles.zimmermann.com`), GA4/Meta/etc. Out of FED scope. |

**Hold this:** FED implements emission per the DD. FED does **not** author the dictionary and does **not** build TNL's GTM-side consumption utility. FED **can** table a straw-man schema (`13-gtm.md §5`, GA4 conventions) as the starting point — repo openItems §13.2 frames it as "storefront proposes, TNL confirms."

## Ground truth to state plainly
Nothing on this surface is built — it's greenfield (grep-verified: no dataLayer/GTM/Didomi/Optimizely/CrazyEgg/Emarsys/Omneo code; env placeholders present but unread; only live tracking = OOTB Einstein `sendViewPage`). Scheduled **Sprint 7 (last), Squad B**. The "mid-Aug / first-month-of-build" date is a **13-07 estimate, not committed** — but the tension is real: TNL is blocked on the DD, and the DD-dependent emission is parked last.

## Non-negotiables to keep crisp
1. **Data layer fires regardless of consent** (AAB-003) — it's first-party SFCC state, not a 3rd-party script. **Didomi gates the tags (in GTM), not the data layer.** (Most likely point to get muddled.)
2. **Optimizely + Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM** (confirmed 09-06) — PWA-direct head tags, Didomi-gated (Optimizely US-only, one snippet, Zimm supplies script). Prod scripts already received (30-Jun); non-prod IDs outstanding.
3. **Crazy Egg masking:** FED renders maskable fields with **stable selectors** + emits data layer; **TNL owns the payment/PII masking config inside Crazy Egg** (openItems §16.2). Get that confirmed.
4. **Enhanced Conversions:** FED emits SHA-256 hashed email at `purchase` (REG-056). No raw PII, no card data ever in the data layer.

## Questions to drive (mapped to their agenda)
- **DD overview:** ~150 event rows today — **which survive the re-platform?** Can't scope SFCC-553 until the culled "Events" tab is locked.
- **DD publication:** publish final DD to **Confluence** + link each event to its owning story (Tim's 13-07 action, still open — owners Andrew/Vicky). *Is it being published from this session?*
- **Ownership sign-off:** get the 3-layer model above **explicitly confirmed** (Copilot key-action #2 = "data-layer design ownership still needs confirmation").
- **Schema confirmation:** does our GA4-conventions schema satisfy GTM's tags **and** any Optimizely (AAB-004) / Crazy Egg (AAB-005) needs? TNL previously suspected **no SFCC-side work needed for Optimizely** (Magento was GTM-only) — confirm before we build segmentation attributes.
- **Addingwell/GTM loading model:** non-prod first-party tagging-server hosts still to be provisioned; per-env container IDs **or** confirmation loading routes via Addingwell so IDs may not be PWA-side.
- **Didomi IDs:** purpose/vendor IDs + per-env Notice IDs — **all TBC**; blocks SFCC-107 (Didomi SDK) → SFCC-106 (consent gating).
- **Attribute sourcing:** LTV, loyalty status, customer group, existing-customer flag, region (Zimm geo **+** Global-e) — where does the PWA source these at runtime? Real dependency (Omneo/loyalty/Global-e).
- **CSP:** `contentSecurityPolicy.ts` (**Tier 1**) doesn't yet allow GTM/Addingwell/Optimizely/CrazyEgg — a gated change, flag it.

## Conflict to surface: Inside Chat (SFCC-581) — documented 3 ways
- Repo `openItems §14` + TSD: **PWA-direct head tag** (confirmed 2026-07-10).
- JIRA **SFCC-581** (updated 06-Aug): PWA pushes a **data-layer event** so the widget inits **via Addingwell/GTM**.

→ Three positions (direct head tag / GTM-loaded + PWA data-layer push / no PWA work). **Ask for one confirmed position.** Magento today = hardcoded Tryzens `Tryzens_ExtendInsideChat` head script; SPA has no full page reloads, so the old approach doesn't map cleanly.

## Don't conflate
**Analytics data layer** (TNL, doc 13) vs **SEO JSON-LD structured data** (Sparro, `sparroSchema.md`) — different artefacts, different owners. TNL = analytics; Sparro = SEO.

## What FED can commit to today
- Implement emission to the DD once finalised; table `13-gtm.md §5` as the straw-man now.
- Validate implementability (SPA route-change events, SSR, attribute availability) as TNL walks the DD.
- Render maskable fields with stable selectors for Crazy Egg.
- **Decouple spec (now) from build (per-page across Sprints 2–6 + consolidation in 7)** — emission points get built as PDP/PLP/cart/checkout are built; it can't be one late story.

## Top asks to leave with (next steps)
1. Final DD → Confluence, event→story linkage. (Andrew/Vicky)
2. Culled final event list locked. (TNL)
3. Ownership model signed off in writing. (all)
4. Schema confirmed for GTM + Optimizely/CrazyEgg. (TNL)
5. Non-prod Addingwell hosts + container-ID model. (Zimm/ACN/TNL)

1	# 12 — Didomi (Consent Management Platform)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Didomi is the Consent Management Platform (CMP) for all seven Zimmermann storefronts. It is the gatekeeper for every third-party script that loads in the browser — marketing tags, analytics tags, heatmap and session-replay tools, the live-chat widget, the Adyen Drop-in, the Narvar EDD widget, and Google reCAPTCHA all wait on a Didomi signal before initialising.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- First-load cookie banner and consent UI
10	- Persistence of consent choices across sessions and pages
11	- Re-prompt and preference-centre access
12	- Consent callbacks consumed by application code to gate downstream scripts
13	- Google Consent Mode v2 signal emission (`ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization`, `analytics_storage`)
14	
15	Out of scope of this document:
16	
17	- The downstream tags themselves — owned by Tell No Lies inside the GTM container
18	- Server-side consent recording or back-office reporting
19	
20	## 2. Browser-side architecture
21	
22	```
23	First page load
24	        │
25	        ▼
26	@didomi/react component mounted at the top of the React tree
27	   (which injects Didomi loader from sdk.privacy-center.org)
28	        │
29	        ▼
30	Didomi SDK initialises ─────► reads persisted consent (cookie + localStorage)
31	        │
32	        ├── consent already given → fires consent.changed immediately
33	        │           │
34	        │           ▼
35	        │     App listeners load gated scripts (GTM, Inside Chat,
36	        │     Narvar EDD widget, Adyen, reCAPTCHA, etc.)
37	        │
38	        └── no prior consent → Didomi renders the banner
39	                    │
40	                    ▼
41	                User makes a choice
42	                    │
43	                    ▼
44	                consent.changed event fires with the new purpose and vendor IDs
45	```
46	
47	- The PWA uses the **`@didomi/react`** package to mount the SDK as early as possible at the top of the React tree. This is the Didomi-recommended approach for SPAs and keeps configuration tied to a single component rather than a raw script tag.
48	- The SDK's loader is fetched asynchronously from `sdk.privacy-center.org`. Configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is pulled from the Didomi Console at runtime — the loader URL itself is environment-agnostic; the per-environment Notice ID identifies the configuration.
49	- The PWA registers listeners for `consent.changed` and per-vendor status changes. Each gated integration subscribes to the specific purpose or vendor ID it requires; on grant, it dynamically imports or injects its script tag.
50	- SSR HTML must not contain markup whose presence or content depends on consent state — consent-driven UI is hydrated on the client. This keeps the SSR cache consent-agnostic and avoids cumulative layout shift.
51	- No consent rules are hard-coded in the storefront. All configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is owned by the Privacy team in the Didomi Console.
52	
53	## 3. Credentials
54	
55	- **Public credential:** the Didomi Notice ID, embedded in the `@didomi/react` component props. Safe to ship in the browser bundle.
56	- **No machine credential is required from the storefront** — the SDK authenticates using the Notice ID alone.
57	- **Per-environment Notice IDs:** separate Didomi Notices are provisioned per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) so non-production traffic never affects production consent reporting. The PWA reads the active Notice ID from an environment variable resolved at build / runtime.
58	
59	## 4. Data exchanged
60	
61	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| Browser → Didomi | None at runtime — consent UI is rendered by the SDK from the Console configuration | n/a |
64	| Didomi → Browser | Consent state: per-purpose booleans, per-vendor booleans, IAB TCF string, regulation applied, opaque user ID | `consent.changed` event and `Didomi.getCurrentUserStatus()` |
65	| Browser → GTM dataLayer | Default and updated Consent Mode v2 signals | `gtag('consent', 'default' \| 'update', …)` |
66	
67	The storefront does not pass PII to Didomi. The Didomi user ID is an opaque consent identifier — it is not joined to the SFCC customer profile and is never written to the customer record.
68	
69	## 5. Consent and gating contract
70	
71	Every PWA-direct integration that loads a third-party script subscribes to one of the buckets below. The storefront's configurable consent categories are **Performance, Analytics, and Marketing**, with **Required** always granted (REG-051). The exact Didomi purpose IDs used in production are owned by the Privacy team in the Console; the table is the application-side mapping.
72	
73	| Bucket | Purpose family | Scripts gated |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Required (strictly necessary) | Always granted, no banner consent | Didomi itself; SFCC SCAPI; Contentful Delivery API; PWA→MRT proxy reads; Adyen Drop-in — **not Didomi consent-gated**: payment is strictly necessary and the Drop-in loads at the payment step regardless of consent state. The fail-closed rule (§8) applies to analytics/marketing scripts, not payment. |
76	| Analytics / measurement | `analytics`, `measure_content_performance` | GTM analytics tags (GA4 and anything Tell No Lies routes to it); Crazy Egg (all storefronts — AAB-005) and Optimizely Web (US storefront only — AAB-004) — both frontend-direct scripts, not in GTM. **Consent categories are TBC — Zimmermann to confirm** |
77	| Marketing / advertising | `create_ads_profile`, `select_personalized_ads`, `targeted_advertising` | Meta Pixel, GTM marketing tags, Enhanced Conversions |
78	| Performance | `improve_products`, `personalize_content` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD **(TBC)**, Google Maps address autocomplete, Inside Chat **(TBC — consent category to be confirmed with Tell No Lies)**, Omneo widget (vendor disclosure only) |
79	| reCAPTCHA | **EU & UK: consent-gated (TBC)** — loads only post-consent in those regions; no consent required on other storefronts at form interaction | Google reCAPTCHA site-key load on the relevant forms |
80	
81	Adyen is a payment necessity and defers load until the customer reaches checkout, so it does not contribute to LCP on any other page. reCAPTCHA likewise defers until register / login form interaction — it loads with no consent requirement in most regions, and is consent-gated in EU & UK (TBC), providing no bot protection where consent is ignored/declined.
82	
83	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
84	
85	- The Didomi loader is fetched asynchronously and is small (Didomi-reported figures put it in the low single-digit KB range gzipped).
86	- Per HPC-013/014 the Didomi notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes. The underlying LCP candidate (the hero image) still renders behind the scrim, so LCP is measured normally; the page is simply non-interactive until the shopper completes the flow. The grey-out is a confirmed requirement (subject to final designs) — the notice is not deferred away.
87	- All downstream gated scripts are deferred behind their consent callback and dynamically imported / injected. None contribute to the LCP measurement on any page — **with one deliberate, scoped exception: Optimizely Web**. On the US storefront only (per AAB-004), Optimizely is head-loaded before render so its anti-flicker snippet can suppress content flash; this exception is allowed to take priority over the LCP budget. Crazy Egg has no such carve-out and must not block LCP.
88	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to `sdk.privacy-center.org` is emitted in the document head so the SDK fetch does not pay a cold DNS / TLS cost.
89	
90	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
91	
92	- A single Didomi Notice serves all eight storefronts; per-region purpose configuration is managed inside the Didomi Console. The Notice ID does not vary by region — Didomi auto-detects the applicable regulation from the visitor's IP.
93	- Per-region default consent state follows REG-054: EU storefronts opted-out; US domestic requires an explicit choice (no action = opted-out); AU, US international, HK, and ME are opted-in by default. These defaults are configured in the Didomi Console and honoured by the SDK when it loads. The fail-closed rule in §8 applies only when consent state cannot be determined (SDK load failure) and is independent of these per-region defaults.
94	- The marketing opt-in checkbox at registration and newsletter sign-up is **a separate UI control from the Didomi banner** and follows the regional defaults in the Functional Requirements (REG-057): pre-checked on US domestic only, unchecked everywhere else.
95	- The banner language follows the active storefront locale: English for AU, UK, US, HK, ME, and EU international; English, French, Italian, or Spanish for EU domestic. A storefront locale switch triggers `Didomi.setUserLanguage()` so the preference centre also renders in the new language.
96	- **Open (TBD):** consent behaviour on the Global-e-owned checkout iframe origin is not yet settled — how (or whether) Didomi consent state propagates to that cross-origin context remains to be confirmed.
97	
98	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
99	
100	| Failure | Behaviour |
101	|---|---|

# 12 — Didomi (Consent Management Platform)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Didomi is the Consent Management Platform (CMP) for all seven Zimmermann storefronts. It is the gatekeeper for every third-party script that loads in the browser — marketing tags, analytics tags, heatmap and session-replay tools, the live-chat widget, the Adyen Drop-in, the Narvar EDD widget, and Google reCAPTCHA all wait on a Didomi signal before initialising.

In scope:

- First-load cookie banner and consent UI
- Persistence of consent choices across sessions and pages
- Re-prompt and preference-centre access
- Consent callbacks consumed by application code to gate downstream scripts
- Google Consent Mode v2 signal emission (`ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization`, `analytics_storage`)

Out of scope of this document:

- The downstream tags themselves — owned by Tell No Lies inside the GTM container
- Server-side consent recording or back-office reporting

## 2. Browser-side architecture

```
First page load
        │
        ▼
@didomi/react component mounted at the top of the React tree
   (which injects Didomi loader from sdk.privacy-center.org)
        │
        ▼
Didomi SDK initialises ─────► reads persisted consent (cookie + localStorage)
        │
        ├── consent already given → fires consent.changed immediately
        │           │
        │           ▼
        │     App listeners load gated scripts (GTM, Inside Chat,
        │     Narvar EDD widget, Adyen, reCAPTCHA, etc.)
        │
        └── no prior consent → Didomi renders the banner
                    │
                    ▼
                User makes a choice
                    │
                    ▼
                consent.changed event fires with the new purpose and vendor IDs
```

- The PWA uses the **`@didomi/react`** package to mount the SDK as early as possible at the top of the React tree. This is the Didomi-recommended approach for SPAs and keeps configuration tied to a single component rather than a raw script tag.
- The SDK's loader is fetched asynchronously from `sdk.privacy-center.org`. Configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is pulled from the Didomi Console at runtime — the loader URL itself is environment-agnostic; the per-environment Notice ID identifies the configuration.
- The PWA registers listeners for `consent.changed` and per-vendor status changes. Each gated integration subscribes to the specific purpose or vendor ID it requires; on grant, it dynamically imports or injects its script tag.
- SSR HTML must not contain markup whose presence or content depends on consent state — consent-driven UI is hydrated on the client. This keeps the SSR cache consent-agnostic and avoids cumulative layout shift.
- No consent rules are hard-coded in the storefront. All configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is owned by the Privacy team in the Didomi Console.

## 3. Credentials

- **Public credential:** the Didomi Notice ID, embedded in the `@didomi/react` component props. Safe to ship in the browser bundle.
- **No machine credential is required from the storefront** — the SDK authenticates using the Notice ID alone.
- **Per-environment Notice IDs:** separate Didomi Notices are provisioned per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) so non-production traffic never affects production consent reporting. The PWA reads the active Notice ID from an environment variable resolved at build / runtime.

## 4. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Browser → Didomi | None at runtime — consent UI is rendered by the SDK from the Console configuration | n/a |
| Didomi → Browser | Consent state: per-purpose booleans, per-vendor booleans, IAB TCF string, regulation applied, opaque user ID | `consent.changed` event and `Didomi.getCurrentUserStatus()` |
| Browser → GTM dataLayer | Default and updated Consent Mode v2 signals | `gtag('consent', 'default' \| 'update', …)` |

The storefront does not pass PII to Didomi. The Didomi user ID is an opaque consent identifier — it is not joined to the SFCC customer profile and is never written to the customer record.

## 5. Consent and gating contract

Every PWA-direct integration that loads a third-party script subscribes to one of the buckets below. The storefront's configurable consent categories are **Performance, Analytics, and Marketing**, with **Required** always granted (REG-051). The exact Didomi purpose IDs used in production are owned by the Privacy team in the Console; the table is the application-side mapping.

| Bucket | Purpose family | Scripts gated |
|---|---|---|
| Required (strictly necessary) | Always granted, no banner consent | Didomi itself; SFCC SCAPI; Contentful Delivery API; PWA→MRT proxy reads; Adyen Drop-in — **not Didomi consent-gated**: payment is strictly necessary and the Drop-in loads at the payment step regardless of consent state. The fail-closed rule (§8) applies to analytics/marketing scripts, not payment. |
| Analytics / measurement | `analytics`, `measure_content_performance` | GTM analytics tags (GA4 and anything Tell No Lies routes to it); Crazy Egg (all storefronts — AAB-005) and Optimizely Web (US storefront only — AAB-004) — both frontend-direct scripts, not in GTM. **Consent categories are TBC — Zimmermann to confirm** |
| Marketing / advertising | `create_ads_profile`, `select_personalized_ads`, `targeted_advertising` | Meta Pixel, GTM marketing tags, Enhanced Conversions |
| Performance | `improve_products`, `personalize_content` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD **(TBC)**, Google Maps address autocomplete, Inside Chat **(TBC — consent category to be confirmed with Tell No Lies)**, Omneo widget (vendor disclosure only) |
| reCAPTCHA | **EU & UK: consent-gated (TBC)** — loads only post-consent in those regions; no consent required on other storefronts at form interaction | Google reCAPTCHA site-key load on the relevant forms |

Adyen is a payment necessity and defers load until the customer reaches checkout, so it does not contribute to LCP on any other page. reCAPTCHA likewise defers until register / login form interaction — it loads with no consent requirement in most regions, and is consent-gated in EU & UK (TBC), providing no bot protection where consent is ignored/declined.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- The Didomi loader is fetched asynchronously and is small (Didomi-reported figures put it in the low single-digit KB range gzipped).
- Per HPC-013/014 the Didomi notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes. The underlying LCP candidate (the hero image) still renders behind the scrim, so LCP is measured normally; the page is simply non-interactive until the shopper completes the flow. The grey-out is a confirmed requirement (subject to final designs) — the notice is not deferred away.
- All downstream gated scripts are deferred behind their consent callback and dynamically imported / injected. None contribute to the LCP measurement on any page — **with one deliberate, scoped exception: Optimizely Web**. On the US storefront only (per AAB-004), Optimizely is head-loaded before render so its anti-flicker snippet can suppress content flash; this exception is allowed to take priority over the LCP budget. Crazy Egg has no such carve-out and must not block LCP.
- `<link rel="preconnect">` to `sdk.privacy-center.org` is emitted in the document head so the SDK fetch does not pay a cold DNS / TLS cost.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Didomi Notice serves all eight storefronts; per-region purpose configuration is managed inside the Didomi Console. The Notice ID does not vary by region — Didomi auto-detects the applicable regulation from the visitor's IP.
- Per-region default consent state follows REG-054: EU storefronts opted-out; US domestic requires an explicit choice (no action = opted-out); AU, US international, HK, and ME are opted-in by default. These defaults are configured in the Didomi Console and honoured by the SDK when it loads. The fail-closed rule in §8 applies only when consent state cannot be determined (SDK load failure) and is independent of these per-region defaults.
- The marketing opt-in checkbox at registration and newsletter sign-up is **a separate UI control from the Didomi banner** and follows the regional defaults in the Functional Requirements (REG-057): pre-checked on US domestic only, unchecked everywhere else.
- The banner language follows the active storefront locale: English for AU, UK, US, HK, ME, and EU international; English, French, Italian, or Spanish for EU domestic. A storefront locale switch triggers `Didomi.setUserLanguage()` so the preference centre also renders in the new language.
- **Open (TBD):** consent behaviour on the Global-e-owned checkout iframe origin is not yet settled — how (or whether) Didomi consent state propagates to that cross-origin context remains to be confirmed.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Didomi loader fails to fetch (CDN outage, network block, blocker extension) | **Fail closed.** The Didomi Web SDK does not itself default to denied if it fails to load — the storefront implements a 5-second timeout (a project decision, not a Didomi-recommended value). On timeout, the storefront acts as if no consent has been granted: GCM signals stay denied, no gated scripts load. The storefront remains functional for browsing and for SFCC checkout. |
| Didomi loader loads but `consent.changed` never fires (SDK initialisation bug, blocked storage) | Same as above — fail closed after the 5-second timeout; the error is logged to monitoring. |
| Consent is granted but a downstream script fails to load | The page does not block. The failure is logged. The customer experience continues. |
| User revokes consent mid-session | Previously-loaded gated scripts are signalled to disable where the vendor supports it (e.g. GTM `gtag('consent', 'update', …)`). For vendors with no runtime disable, scripts remain in memory but receive no further events; full cleanup happens on the next page navigation. |
| User in a region where Didomi has misclassified the regulation | The preference centre is always reachable from the footer "Cookie preferences" link; the customer can adjust manually. |

## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.

Zimmermann uses **Didomi** as its Consent Management Platform (CMP). When a shopper first visits the site they see a bottom-of-page banner ("Agree and Close" / "Edit Preferences" / "Continue without agreeing"). If they click "Edit Preferences", Didomi's own preference centre opens — a modal where they can toggle consent per category.

**Didomi manages** (not Accenture's build scope): - The banner UI and preference centre - Storage of the shopper's consent record - Consent renewal, expiry, and regional default behaviour - Serving different consent defaults per region (carried over from current Magento configuration)
